searchText: This is interesting! I am thinking how safe it is to drop chunks of any aggregate before a node received enough chunks to recover a message with a greedier aggregate. Btw, with staggered aggregate publishing this may work smoother. so the way i am processing the chunks currently is: - 1st aggregate for committee: store chunks and forward - subsequent: check if already have superset -- if yes, receive but do not forward further chunks -- if no, receive as normal - then if original aggregate fails to decode or validate, start forwarding again as I wrote that I realised there are some thing missing: a new aggregate that is 'better' should replace the existing 'active' aggregate; if the 'best' fails it should pick the next best for forwarding etc. until the best aggregate you ever observed has enough chunks, you have to keep the 2nd best aggregate chunks, and so on keep but do not forward doesn't that mean that i can send a single chunk with super nice aggregate and brick dissemination of aggregates with less bits? you could, but we keep receiving the others and if one completes and passes validation we forward it (like we would for gossip) so you can slow throughput - probably something that needs scoring penalties. for the 'held' aggregates I continue receiving but do not forward unless it completes and validates. right, but if a chunk of a greedier aggregate has been received by everyone in the network before others, why would anyone except for publishers broadcast chunks of less greedy ones? for the same reason - one chunk isn't the whole aggregate, so best to keep accepting chunks for other aggregates. so fast diffusion is optimistic - it forwards what appears to be the best, but forwards what is actually best once it has a full aggregate (if that is different). TBH the aggregation dissemination pattern even without respect to superset filtering (just networking layer) is kind of not very responsible to chunking and other techniques successfully used in SeaCast for e.g. payload. In my simulations the plain Gossip still has either close or even better latency for 64 aggregates dissemination. Throughput is still around x2 though. I'm still not sure if my simulations are 100% reliable and would like to see others confirmations. were you forwarding chunks for all aggregates? that gives worse outcome than plain gossip - see the original message above. if I handle aggregates with seacast using the approach described in this thread it saves 50% of bandwidth. you have to have superset filtering in the network layer basically or superset driven deferred forwarding to be more precise Yes, just a naive chunking didn't make things better comparing to a one-chunk gossip for me. I would say it made the latency slightly worse and increase throughput significantly I saw the same initially. Superset filtering is handled on the application layer basically. For the pure network your messages are opaque. So I didn't consider filtering in my sims yet so i added the validator bitset to the chunk metadata so it can be checked as part of chunk validation and based on the check, chunks are 'held' or forwarded. in my sim where probably all the aggregates contain the same votes, I went from forwarding all aggregates to forwarding 1. Right, it could be the case actually.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
This is interesting! I am thinking how safe it is to drop chunks of any aggregate before a node received enough chunks to recover a message with a greedier aggregate.

Btw, with staggered aggregate publishing this may work smoother.

excerpts.author: vladimir_ea
excerpts.content:
so the way i am processing the chunks currently is:
- 1st aggregate for committee: store chunks and forward
- subsequent: check if already have superset
   -- if yes, receive but do not forward further chunks
   -- if no, receive as normal
- then if original aggregate fails to decode or validate, start forwarding again

as I wrote that I realised there are some thing missing: a new aggregate that is 'better' should replace the existing 'active' aggregate; if the 'best' fails it should pick the next best for forwarding etc.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: until the best aggregate you ever observed has enough chunks, you have to keep the 2nd best aggregate chunks, and so on

excerpts.author: vladimir_ea
excerpts.content: keep but do not forward

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: doesn't that mean that i can send a single chunk with super nice aggregate and brick dissemination of aggregates with less bits?

excerpts.author: vladimir_ea
excerpts.content: you could, but we keep receiving the others and if one completes and passes validation we forward it (like we would for gossip)

excerpts.author: vladimir_ea
excerpts.content: so you can slow throughput - probably something that needs scoring penalties.

excerpts.author: vladimir_ea
excerpts.content: for the 'held' aggregates I continue receiving but do not forward unless it completes and validates.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: right, but if a chunk of a greedier aggregate has been received by everyone in the network before others, why would anyone except for publishers broadcast chunks of less greedy ones?

excerpts.author: vladimir_ea
excerpts.content: for the same reason - one chunk isn't the whole aggregate, so best to keep accepting chunks for other aggregates.

excerpts.author: vladimir_ea
excerpts.content: so fast diffusion is optimistic - it forwards what appears to be the best, but forwards what is actually best once it has a full aggregate (if that is different).

excerpts.author: nashatyrev
excerpts.content:
TBH the aggregation dissemination pattern even without respect to superset filtering (just networking layer) is kind of not very responsible to chunking and other techniques successfully used in SeaCast for e.g. payload. In my simulations the plain Gossip still has either close or even better latency for 64 aggregates dissemination. Throughput is still around x2 though. 

I'm still not sure if my simulations are 100% reliable and would like to see others confirmations.

were you forwarding chunks for all aggregates? that gives worse outcome than plain gossip - see the original message above.

if I handle aggregates with seacast using the approach described in this thread it saves 50% of bandwidth.
